automotive.rolling_resistance.title: Rolling resistance force (F = C_rr·N)

variables.name: N
variables.desc: normal load on the driven tyres

assumptions: C_rr is a tyre-road input (tyre maker or road-test data); it rises slightly with speed and inflation pressure, treated constant here.

automotive.road_load.title: Tractive effort and road-load power (rolling + aero + grade)

variables.name: F_t
variables.desc: tractive effort required at the wheels (negative downhill)

variables.name: P_req
variables.desc: road-load power required (F_t·v; negative when descending)

assumptions: Steady speed on a constant grade; no headwind. θ is signed: positive = uphill, negative = downhill (on a steep enough descent gravity overcomes drag + rolling resistance, so F_t and P_req go negative — the vehicle needs braking, not drive). F_t is the traction demand, not the tyre limit (that needs the available tractive force, see tractive_effort / gradeability).
method_references: Road-load equation F = C_rr·W·cosθ + ½ρCdAv² + W·sinθ

automotive.gradeability.title: Maximum grade from available tractive effort
assumptions: Low-speed climb (aerodynamic drag neglected). The equilibrium on a grade is W·sinθ + C_rr·W·cosθ = F_avail, solved exactly as θ = asin((F_avail/W)/√(1 + C_rr²)) − atan(C_rr) — consistent with the cosθ rolling term in road_load. F_avail is the lesser of engine-traction and tyre-adhesion limit; valid for F_avail/W ≤ √(1 + C_rr²).
method_references: Equilibrium on a grade: W·sinθ + C_rr·W·cosθ = F_avail

automotive.acceleration.title: Longitudinal acceleration from excess tractive force
assumptions: Flat road, one value of resistance at the instant considered (get F_rr from rolling_resistance, F_d from fluid_dynamics.drag_lift, or F_t directly from road_load). k_m accounts for rotating inertia (≈ 1.04–1.10 in low gears).
method_references: Newton's second law with effective (rotating) mass

automotive.top_speed.title: Top speed from an engine torque curve and gear ratios

variables.name: gear_ratios
variables.desc: overall gear ratios (transmission x final drive), one per gear

variables.name: gear_at_top
variables.desc: gear (1-based) that reaches the top speed

procedure.python:
def _top_speed(values):
    """Top speed: largest speed where the best tractive force (over all gears whose engine speed is inside
    the torque curve) meets the road load, or the top-gear redline speed if force still exceeds it there.

    At each speed only gears with w_min <= v·i/r_w <= w_max contribute; the best gear is the one giving the
    largest tractive force. Below the first gear's idle speed no gear can pull (clutch-slip region), so the
    crossing is sought above that speed. The top speed is the first speed where the best force falls below
    road load; if the force is still above road load at the top-gear redline, the top speed is redline-limited.
    """
    curve = values['torque_curve']
    ratios = values['gear_ratios']
    if not isinstance(curve, list) or len(curve) < 2:
        raise MechError('torque_curve: give [[rpm, N*m], ...] with at least 2 points')
    if not isinstance(ratios, list) or not ratios:
        raise MechError('gear_ratios: give a non-empty list of overall (transmission x final drive) ratios')
    rows = []
    for r in curve:
        if not isinstance(r, (list, tuple)) or len(r) != 2:
            raise MechError('torque_curve rows must be [rpm, N*m]')
        rows.append((float(r[0]), float(r[1])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda t: t[0])
    rpm = np.array([t[0] for t in rows], dtype=float)
    tor = np.array([t[1] for t in rows], dtype=float)
    if rpm[0] <= 0 or np.any(np.diff(rpm) <= 0):
        raise MechError('torque_curve engine speeds must be positive and strictly increasing')
    ratios = [float(i) for i in ratios]
    if any(i <= 0 for i in ratios):
        raise MechError('gear_ratios must be positive')
    w_curve = rpm * (2 * PI / 60)          # rad/s; redline = top of the torque curve
    w_min, w_max = w_curve[0], w_curve[-1]
    rw, m, Cd, A = values['r_wheel'], values['m'], values['Cd'], values['A']
    Crr, rho, eta, g = values['C_rr'], values['rho'], values['eta_driveline'], values['g']
    F_roll = Crr * m * g
    i_top = min(ratios)                     # top gear = smallest overall ratio
    v_red_top = w_max * rw / i_top

    def road(v):
        return F_roll + 0.5 * rho * Cd * A * v * v

    def gear_force(v, ig):
        """Tractive force of one gear, or -inf when the engine speed is outside the torque curve."""
        we = v * ig / rw
        if we < w_min or we > w_max:
            return float('-inf')
        return eta * float(np.interp(we, w_curve, tor)) * ig / rw

    def best_force(v):
        return max(gear_force(v, ig) for ig in ratios)

    v = np.linspace(0.0, v_red_top, 1200)
    ex = np.array([best_force(x) - road(x) for x in v])
    moving = [k for k in range(len(v)) if ex[k] >= 0.0]
    if not moving:
        raise MechError('no solution: available tractive effort never exceeds the road load')
    start = moving[0]
    cross = None
    for k in range(start, len(v) - 1):
        if ex[k] >= 0.0 and ex[k + 1] < 0.0:
            cross = k
            break
    if cross is None:
        vmax, redline = v_red_top, True
    else:
        a, b = v[cross], v[cross + 1]
        for _ in range(80):                 # bisect the force balance at the crossing
            mid = 0.5 * (a + b)
            if best_force(mid) - road(mid) >= 0.0:
                a = mid
            else:
                b = mid
        vmax, redline = 0.5 * (a + b), False
    kbest = max(range(len(ratios)), key=lambda k: gear_force(vmax, ratios[k]))
    i_best = ratios[kbest]
    F_top = gear_force(vmax, i_best)
    out = {'v_max': vmax,
           'P_max_wheel': F_top * vmax,
           'gear_at_top': float(kbest + 1),    # 1-based gear number
           'omega_e_top': min(vmax * i_best / rw, w_max)}
    if redline:
        out['_warnings'] = ['top speed is at the engine redline in the top (longest) gear '
                            '(speed-limited rather than drag-limited)']
    return out

assumptions: At each speed the best tractive force is taken over every gear whose engine speed is inside the torque curve; the top speed is the first speed where that best force falls below the road load, or the top-gear (smallest-ratio) redline speed if force still exceeds it there. The torque curve is interpolated linearly between points; below the first gear's idle speed no gear can pull (the clutch slips), so the crossing is sought above it. A redline-limited result is reported with a warning.
method_references: Power available (η·T·ω) = power required ((C_rr·m·g + ½ρCdAv²)·v) at the top speed

automotive.gear_ratio.title: Gear pair: torque and speed through a reduction
assumptions: Single mesh with efficiency η; i > 1 reduces speed and multiplies torque.
method_references: Ideal gear power balance: T_out·ω_out = η·T_in·ω_in

automotive.vehicle_speed.title: Vehicle speed from engine speed and overall gear ratio
assumptions: No tyre slip (drive wheels roll without slipping).

automotive.tractive_effort.title: Tractive effort at the wheels from engine torque

variables.name: F_t
variables.desc: tractive effort at the driven wheels

assumptions: Overall ratio i_g·i_d from the engine to the wheels, with driveline efficiency η; no tyre slip. This is the engine-side tractive effort — compare with road_load to see whether the vehicle can accelerate at a given speed.

automotive.engine_power.title: Engine power required from wheel power
assumptions: The engine must deliver P_wheel/η to overcome a road-load power P_wheel at the wheels (the driveline dissipates (1 − η)·P_eng). Get P_wheel from road_load.

automotive.braking_distance.title: Braking distance with reaction time (flat road)

variables.name: mu
variables.desc: tyre-road friction coefficient (all wheels at the limit)
variables.label: μ

variables.name: t_r
variables.desc: driver reaction time (distance travelled before braking)

assumptions: All wheels braked at the adhesion limit (μ); flat, dry-road single value. d = v·t_r (reaction) + v²/(2μg) (braking). On a grade, replace μ·g by g·(μ·cosθ + sinθ) for braking uphill.
method_references: Constant-deceleration kinematics: d = v·t_r + v²/(2a) with a = μg

automotive.weight_transfer.title: Longitudinal weight transfer and dynamic axle loads

variables.name: l_f
variables.desc: front axle to centre of gravity

variables.name: l_r
variables.desc: rear axle to centre of gravity

assumptions: Rigid vehicle, quasi-static transfer, small pitch (CG height taken constant). A negative dynamic axle load means that axle has lifted off — the vehicle is about to tip.
method_references: Moment equilibrium about the axles: ΔW = m·a·h/L

automotive.brake_distribution.title: Brake force distribution from vehicle geometry (ideal split)

variables.name: a_g
variables.desc: braking deceleration in g (= μ at the adhesion limit)

variables.name: delta_W
variables.desc: longitudinal load transfer to the front axle
variables.label: ΔW

variables.name: front_frac
variables.desc: front fraction of total brake force

variables.name: l_f
variables.desc: front axle to centre of gravity

variables.name: l_r
variables.desc: rear axle to centre of gravity

variables.name: mu
variables.desc: tyre-road friction coefficient (deceleration in g at the limit)
variables.label: μ

assumptions: Ideal (both axles at lockup simultaneously): the braking deceleration in g equals the friction coefficient (a_g = μ), the front axle gains ΔW = W·a_g·h/L, and each axle carries μ × its dynamic load. The front fraction (l_r + μ·h)/L is the brake bias that locks both axles together. Real proportioning valves bias toward the front and fall below this ideal line.
method_references: Brake force proportional to dynamic normal load at each axle; front fraction (l_r + μ·h)/L

automotive.tyre_lateral_force.title: Tyre lateral force from cornering stiffness (linear model)
assumptions: Linear (small-slip-angle) tyre model: F_y = C_α·α. C_α is a tyre input (N/rad); the model saturates at large slip (α ≳ 5–8°, tyre-specific) where F_y ≈ μ·F_z instead. For the pure centripetal force of a vehicle in a turn see kinetics.centripetal_force.

automotive.understeer_gradient.title: Slip angles and understeer gradient (bicycle model)
assumptions: Linear (small-slip-angle) bicycle model; cornering stiffness C_af, C_ar are axle sums and tyre inputs (N/rad). K_us is the slip-angle difference at a_y = g, i.e. radians per g: positive = understeer, negative = oversteer.
method_references: Bicycle-model slip angles α = W·a_y/(g·C_α); understeer gradient K_us = W_f/C_αf − W_r/C_αr

automotive.rollover_threshold.title: Static rollover (tip-over) threshold

variables.name: a_y_roll
variables.desc: lateral acceleration at the rollover threshold

assumptions: Rigid vehicle, no suspension compliance (the quasi-static tip-over limit). The static stability factor is track/(2h); suspension roll and tyre forces lower the real threshold.
method_references: Moment balance about the outer tyre contact: a_y/g = track/(2h)

automotive.suspension_frequency.title: Ride (bounce) natural frequency with spring and tyre in series

variables.name: k_ride
variables.desc: ride rate (spring and tyre in series)

variables.name: k_s
variables.desc: spring rate at the wheel (spring rate x motion-ratio²)

variables.name: m
variables.desc: sprung mass carried by the axle

assumptions: Single corner quarter-car, undamped. Spring and tyre are springs in series, k_ride = k_s·k_t/(k_s + k_t); k_s is the wheel rate (spring rate × motion-ratio² for a spring not mounted on the wheel centreline).

automotive.fuel_consumption.title: Fuel consumption rate and fuel economy
assumptions: Engine bsfc is a user input (≈ 0.25–0.28 kg/kWh typical SI range); the example uses 250 g/kWh. Steady speed; economy = v/V_dot in m per m³ (multiply by 1e-3 for km/L).
method_references: Fuel mass rate = bsfc·P; economy = distance / fuel volume

source.derivation: Flat torque curve: in top gear (i=3) tractive force F = ηTi/r = 150·3/0.3 = 1500 N constant. Balance 1500 = 0.01·1000·9.81 + ½·1.2·0.3·2·v² = 98.1 + 0.36v² → v = sqrt(1401.9/0.36) = 62.4033 m/s (below the 62.83 m/s redline). Lower gears are redline-limited at 15.7 and 31.4 m/s, so gear 3 wins. P = 1500·62.4033 = 93604.9 W; ωe = v·i/r = 624.03 rad/s

Peaky curve. Gear 3 (i=3.2) reaches its redline at v = 6000·2π/60·0.3/3.2 = 58.9049 m/s, where the engine still makes 320 N·m: tractive 0.9·320·3.2/0.3 = 3072 N vs road load 0.01·1200·9.81 + ½·1.225·0.25·1.8·58.9049² = 1074 N, so the top speed is the gear-3 redline (dense sweep of the best-gear force envelope; gears 1 and 2 redline at 18.85 and 31.42 m/s)

Flat 300 N·m to 7000 rpm. Top gear (i=5.5) reaches its redline at v = 7000·2π/60·0.3/5.5 = 39.9839 m/s with tractive 0.9·300·5.5/0.3 = 4950 N vs road load 0.01·1200·9.81 + ½·1.225·0.25·1.8·39.9839² = 558.4 N, so it is redline-limited (dense sweep confirms 39.9839 m/s in gear 3); P = 4950·39.9839 = 197920 W; ωe = 7000·2π/60 = 733.04 rad/s
Braking is negative acceleration: ΔW = 12000·(−5)·0.5/(9.81·2.6) = −1176.19 N (forward transfer, front axle gains)
Inverse: μ = (front_frac·L − l_r)/h = (0.701923·2.6 − 1.4)/0.5 = (1.825 − 1.4)/0.5 = 0.85 (front_frac given, mu and the remaining outputs solved)
Oversteer case: K_us = 5000/50000 − 9000/50000 = −0.08 rad (negative = oversteer, exercises the signed output)
